imagery_report.label: IAEA satellite imagery: Yongbyon enrichment facility expansion externally complete
imagery_report.headline: IAEA says North Korea has completed external construction on its Yongbyon uranium enrichment facility extension
imagery_report.body: The International Atomic Energy Agency released its Board of Governors report noting satellite imagery shows the external works on a new extension to North Korea's original uranium enrichment building at Yongbyon are complete, while voicing 'serious concern' over the upgrades. Daily NK separately reported that high-resolution satellite imagery of the Pyongsan uranium refinery shows a new chemical storage tank added and a freight train arriving, alongside growing sludge deposits and apparent wastewater discharge toward the Ryesong River. These findings align with the BP Locations tracker note that Yongbyon enrichment expansion has been ongoing since at least April 2026.

bp_locations.name: Yongbyon Nuclear Complex
bp_locations.note: As of April 2026: Enrichment building expansion complete, new centrifuge hall operational. 5 MWe reactor and IRT-2000 both running. Thermal signatures consistent with increased plutonium/HEU production.

bp_locations.name: Sinpo South Shipyard
bp_locations.note: As of May 2025: Hero Kim Kun Ok SLBM submarine exited drydock after 2+ years of fitting-out but was still not operational. New submarine construction begun in separate bay. NK Pro satellite analysis (Oct 20 2026) separately reports North Korea's Nampho Shipyard missed a deadline earlier in Oct 2026 to launch a 5,000-ton naval destroyer, with hull sections visible at two potential outdoor assembly areas. 38 North analysis published Oct 30 documents public display of a vessel described as a 'Tactical Nuclear Attack' submarine. Kim Jong Un inspected Nampho Shipyard on Nov 7 (reported Nov 8 by KCNA), announcing a new warship under construction larger than the destroyer built last year. NK News reported on Nov 6 that North Korea has expanded warship construction to a third shipyard. 38 North published analysis on Nov 11 of the Choe Hyon destroyer and its strategic implications for the West Sea Fleet. NK News identified a second major east-coast naval base project on Nov 13, beyond the Munchon-area site Kim inspected on Nov 12.

bp_locations.name: THAAD Site, Seongju County
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: All 6 THAAD launchers were redeployed to the Middle East amid Iran tensions. At least 2 launchers may have returned to Seongju by late March 2026. Battery operational status remains uncertain. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Sohae Satellite Launch Station
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: 2,500 kN engine test stand firing observed. Two villages razed for facility expansion. New seaport and large assembly building nearing completion. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Punggye-ri Nuclear Test Site
bp_locations.note: As of November 2025: ROK Defense Intelligence Agency assessed Tunnel No. 3 is test-ready and a nuclear test can be conducted at any time upon political decision. Site maintained at high readiness since mid-2024. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Tumangang–Khasan (NK-Russia border)
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: Road bridge construction accelerated, completion target moved to Summer 2026. Passenger rail service resumed mid-2025. Ore and tank car traffic at highest levels since project began. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state. Russian Transport Ministry applications filed November 13, 2026 for a 14-daily-round-trip Vladivostok-Rason bus route over the new vehicle bridge, with experts noting the service will likely transport DPRK workers more than Russian tourists.

bp_locations.name: Sinuiju–Dandong (NK-China border)
bp_locations.note: NK News Planet Labs satellite imagery analyzed through November 15, 2026 confirms trucks filling Sinuiju customs facility from October 16, the day after the New Yalu River Bridge officially opened, with activity peaking October 19–20. A wall of 40-foot containers bearing Maersk and COSCO markings was visible on the Chinese side. Kim Jong Un crossed the New Yalu River Bridge on October 24 during his unannounced visit to Dandong. Daily NK reported November 12 that Chinese truck drivers who relied on side income ferrying parcels across the new bridge are souring on operations due to tighter customs checks and movement controls. Huanghai Automobile's Dandong bus factory announced November 13 it is operating at full capacity following Kim Jong Un's October visit. Daily NK reported November 18 that Sinuiju markets are overflowing with Chinese goods but a severe cash shortage means almost nobody is buying, with vendors describing a 'trading cliff.'

bp_locations.name: Rason SEZ
bp_locations.note: As of November 2025: Chinese businesspeople re-entry to Rason SEZ expanded. Coal exports through Rason at highest levels in years throughout 2025. Arms export berth also active. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea NLL
bp_locations.note: As of September 26, 2025: 140m DPRK merchant vessel Toksong crossed the Northern Limit Line near Baengnyeong Island, advanced 5km south. ROK Navy fired approximately 60 warning shots; vessel retreated after 1 hour. ROK Marine Corps Commandant Gen. Ju Il-suk stated October 20, 2026 that North Korea has made 'various changes' to forces facing South Korea's border islands, with Seoul stepping up surveillance along the maritime border. 38 North satellite imagery published October 29 shows North Korea continuing to install new fencing along its border. North Korean propaganda loudspeakers were visible at two border locations on November 4, 2026 from Odusan Unification Observatory and Key Observatory in Gyeonggi Province. ROK Joint Chiefs confirmed November 6, 2026 that a drifting North Korean fishing vessel was spotted in international waters off Ulleung Island on November 3 and is under investigation.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea PMZ
bp_locations.note: As of January 27-28, 2026: Atlantic Amsterdam (converted oil rig, Chinese aquaculture platform) relocated out of the Provisional Measures Zone to Weihai shipyard following President Lee Jae-myung's Beijing state visit. Two giant aquaculture cages (Shen Lan 1, Shen Lan 2) and 13 buoys remain in the PMZ. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Vostochny/Dunai
bp_locations.note: As of January 2026: Arms shipments slowed due to ice, one Russian vessel (likely Angara or Lady R) visited Rason, docked January 14, 2026 at arms export berth. Cargo routed to Vostochny. Since September 2023: 64 voyages by 4 vessels (Angara, Maria, Maya-1, Lady R) delivered approximately 15,800 containers (approximately 4.2-5.8 million munitions) from Rajin to Vostochny/Dunai. This report is over six months old and may not reflect the current state. Russian Transport Ministry applications filed November 13, 2026 for a Vladivostok-Rason bus route operating 14 daily round trips.

top_stories.headline: Democratic Party formally adopts impeachment of Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae as party line
top_stories.body: The ruling **Democratic Party** voted at a general caucus meeting on Nov. 20 to pursue the impeachment of Supreme Court Chief Justice **Cho Hee-dae**, one day after the Supreme Court overturned former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo's 15-year insurrection sentence and remanded the case to the Seoul High Court. The party cited Cho's handling of the martial law declaration, his earlier decision to send President Lee Jae-myung's election law case back to appeals court, and allegations of improper use of official funds. The DP holds 161 of 300 Assembly seats, enough to pass an impeachment motion without coalition partners, and plans to introduce the motion before year-end.

top_stories.headline: Trump leaves Asia without meeting Kim Jong Un, says encounter will happen 'at some point'
top_stories.body: President **Donald Trump** flew back to Washington on Nov. 20 after the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen without meeting North Korean leader **Kim Jong Un**, despite publicly raising the prospect during his trip. Trump told NBC News: "The relationship is there, but we didn't meet. There were too many meetings. We'll have that meeting at some point." Secretary of State **Marco Rubio** had said days earlier that Trump was "serious" about engaging with Kim, and the Kremlin had indicated Putin would meet Kim if he attended APEC, Kim did not appear.

top_stories.headline: IAEA says North Korea has completed external works on Yongbyon enrichment facility extension
top_stories.body: The International Atomic Energy Agency reported to its Board of Governors that North Korea has completed the external construction on an extension to its original uranium enrichment facility at Yongbyon, voicing "serious concern" over the upgrades. The IAEA report, released Nov. 19, is the latest in a series of assessments documenting the facility's expansion; the BP Locations tracker recorded the enrichment building expansion as complete with a new centrifuge hall operational as of April 2026. Daily NK separately reported that satellite imagery of the Pyongsan uranium refinery shows a new chemical storage tank added alongside a freight train arrival and apparent wastewater discharge toward the Ryesong River.

also_today.body_text: 38 North reports that at a recent national IT exhibition, North Korea displayed what appears to be a domestically developed AI chatbot, marking the country's public entry into generative AI.

also_today.body_text: 38 North publishes an essay arguing the two Koreas should formalize a separation framework, a 'good divorce', rather than pursuing reunification, amid the Lee government's push for peaceful coexistence.

IAEA 'satisfied' with Seoul's cooperation on nuclear-powered submarine project in first report
also_today.body_text: The IAEA told its Board of Governors it was 'satisfied' with South Korea's cooperation on its nuclear-powered submarine development program, maintaining the 'broader conclusion' that all nuclear material in Korea is used for peaceful purposes. This is the IAEA's first report on the program since President Lee and President Trump announced the project.

also_today.headline: Pyongsan uranium refinery adds chemical storage tank; freight train arrives in satellite imagery
also_today.body_text: High-resolution satellite imagery shows North Korea's Pyongsan uranium refinery adding a chemical storage tank and receiving a freight train, suggesting a ramp-up in nuclear material production, alongside growing sludge and apparent wastewater discharge toward the Ryesong River.

business_economy.headline: South Korea's exports hit $1 trillion for first time, riding AI chip boom
business_economy.body_text: South Korea surpassed $1 trillion in annual exports in 2026, becoming the fourth country globally to reach the milestone, after the United States, China, and Germany, driven by AI semiconductor demand. The achievement came 19 years after China reached the same threshold, with the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy citing semiconductors, cosmetics, and food exports as key contributors.

business_economy.headline: KOSPI and KOSDAQ each fall more than 5% as US semiconductor export control fears weigh
business_economy.body_text: South Korean equities suffered steep declines on Nov. 20, KOSPI down *5.21%*, driven by investor concern over potential US tightening of semiconductor export restrictions on China and spillover from US market weakness. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix were among the hardest-hit, with analysts warning the market's AI-chip dependency has become a vulnerability.

business_economy.headline: Bank of Korea last monetary policy meeting of 2026 set for November 26; rate hike to 3.25% seen as likely
business_economy.body_text: Korean financial media report the Bank of Korea's final Monetary Policy Committee meeting of 2026 is scheduled for November 26, with market consensus pointing to a rate increase from 3.00% to 3.25%. The meeting would mark the first back-to-back hike, the first ever at consecutive meetings, if the committee acts.

business_economy.headline: Kakao founder Kim Beom-soo acquitted on appeal over SM Entertainment stock manipulation charges
business_economy.body_text: An appeals court found **Kim Beom-soo**, founder of Kakao, not guilty of stock price manipulation during the 2023 SM Entertainment acquisition battle against Hybe, ruling that "artificial manipulation was unproven." The ruling overturns the lower court finding and removes criminal liability from one of South Korea's largest technology conglomerates.

business_economy.headline: Ministry of Land freezes apartment appraisal market-rate ratio at 69% for 2027
business_economy.body_text: South Korea's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport decided to hold the housing appraisal-to-market-value ratio at 69.0% for 2027, unchanged from 2026, meaning no additional tax burden from the ratio itself. However, areas where property prices have risen will see higher appraisal values and heavier property holding taxes regardless.

northeast_asia.headline: Korea and Japan hold 12th director-general level Middle East policy consultations in Seoul
northeast_asia.body_text: ROK MOFA Director-General Jeong Gwang-yong met Japanese Foreign Ministry Middle East and Africa Bureau Director-General Iwamoto Keiichi on Nov. 20 for the 12th Korea-Japan director-general-level Middle East Policy Consultations, the first since February 2026 when the 11th session was held in Japan. The two sides agreed to continue active information exchange as like-minded partners on Middle East affairs.

northeast_asia.headline: China maintains hardline stance on Taiwan despite Japan PM Takaichi reaffirming 'One China' policy at APEC
northeast_asia.body_text: Chinese President **Xi Jinping** maintained a firm posture on Taiwan in his bilateral meeting with Japan's PM **Takaichi Sanae** at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, even after Takaichi reconfirmed Japan's adherence to the One China policy. The exchange underlines persistent friction in China-Japan relations that shapes the broader US-ROK-Japan trilateral environment.

rok_personnel.position: Commissioner General, Korean National Police Agency
rok_personnel.name: Kim Jong-chul
rok_personnel.detail: President Lee Jae-myung approved Kim Jong-chul's appointment as commissioner general of the Korean National Police Agency on Nov. 20, ending a vacancy of nearly two years. The post had been vacant since the former police chief was suspended in December 2024 in connection with former President Yoon Suk Yeol's failed martial law bid.

rok_government.action: Second inter-agency K-Initiative overseas expansion meeting held under FM Cho's chairmanship
rok_government.detail: Foreign Minister **Cho Hyun** chaired the second inter-ministerial meeting on overseas expansion of the K-Initiative on Nov. 20, attended by representatives from 11 ministries and agencies including MOTIE, MSIT, and DAPA. The K-Initiative frames South Korea's cultural, technological and democratic experiences as a strategic national asset for public diplomacy and global issue leadership.

rok_government.action: MOFA deputy FM meets Uruguayan deputy FM; presses for Korea-Mercosur trade agreement negotiation resumption
rok_government.detail: Deputy Foreign Minister **Park Yoon-joo** met visiting Uruguayan Deputy FM **Valeria Csukasi** at the MOFA building on Nov. 20 and urged Montevideo, as 2026 Mercosur chair and negotiation coordinator, to actively push for resumption of the Korea-Mercosur Trade Agreement talks. Uruguay supplied blankets and financial support to South Korea during the Korean War.

rok_assembly.action: Democracy Meritorious Persons Act passes plenary without People Power Party participation
rok_assembly.detail: The National Assembly passed the Democracy Meritorious Persons Act on Nov. 20 through a ruling Democratic Party-led vote while the People Power Party boycotted the session, calling it a "privilege bill for the pro-democracy movement faction." The bill provides medical and welfare support to victims and bereaved families of pro-democracy movements; it had failed to pass for 26 years.

rok_assembly.action: Air Force Military Academy cadet dismissed after smartphone exam violation; MND briefed Assembly
rok_assembly.detail: The Air Force Military Academy expelled a third-year cadet who covertly photographed exam questions with a smartphone during a first-semester final exam conducted under the academy's honor-system rules, the first publicly confirmed military academy dismissal for a digital exam violation. The Ministry of National Defense confirmed the case on Nov. 20, citing it in context of the wider AI cheating response.

calendar_watch.headline: BOK monetary policy committee, final meeting of 2026

opeds_today.headline: The Value of U.S.-Japan-ROK Trilateralism: A View from the Three Capitals
opeds_today.central_argument: US-Japan-ROK trilateral cooperation has matured into a practical but limited framework, effective in peacetime and crisis management but constrained by political and legal barriers in wartime, and its durability depends on sustaining coordination through ongoing political transitions in all three capitals.
opeds_today.summary: Based on interviews in Washington, Tokyo, and Seoul, the RAND study assesses trilateral cooperation under two crisis scenarios: a North Korean provocation and a Chinese invasion of Taiwan. It finds information-sharing, cyberdefense, and logistics coordination are functional but that legal and political barriers impede wartime integration. The Camp David Summit of 2023 is identified as the paradigm shift the framework now needs to institutionalize.

opeds_today.headline: Toplines: Why and how the United States and its allies should prepare for a limited nuclear attack
opeds_today.central_argument: The risk of North Korea conducting a limited nuclear attack, a strike constrained in scope but lethal, will likely increase over the coming decade, and the United States and its allies are insufficiently prepared to deter and prevail in such a scenario.
opeds_today.summary: The Guardian Tiger III study, based on engagements with over 150 US and allied government, military, and expert stakeholders, identifies cognitive and organizational biases as barriers to nuclear scenario planning. It notes North Korea could plausibly develop additional warhead types within five to ten years, expanding limited nuclear attack options. The report calls for specific allied preparation measures beyond the existing extended deterrence framework.

opeds_today.headline: At APEC, Lee Urges Asia-Pacific Leaders to Back Talks With North Korea
opeds_today.central_argument: President Lee Jae-myung used the APEC platform in Shenzhen to appeal for multilateral support for resuming North Korea dialogue, framing engagement as a regional stability imperative amid the Trump-Kim no-show.
opeds_today.summary: The piece reports Lee made explicit appeals at APEC for fellow leaders to support renewed inter-Korean and US-North Korea talks, using the multilateral venue to advance what Seoul frames as a 'peaceful coexistence' agenda. The appeal came as Trump departed Shenzhen without meeting Kim, leaving the diplomatic track undefined.

korea_world.headline: South Korea's defense industry expands Middle East push, moving beyond arms exports to production and technology cooperation
korea_world.body_text: South Korean defense firms are accelerating a shift in the Middle East from pure arms sales toward production partnerships and technology cooperation agreements, reflecting a broader change in global defense competition dynamics.

korea_world.headline: North Korea and Laos sign protocol on joint economic committee at Mekong-South Korea summit
korea_world.body_text: North Korea and Laos signed a protocol on a joint economic committee, Yonhap reported from the Mekong-South Korea summit, where Laos also called for stronger digital and green cooperation with Seoul.
